title: Query Parser & Planner
overview:
In this project you will extend the SQL parser and query planner to support **GROUP BY**, **ORDER BY**, and **aggregate functions** (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX).

The existing parser handles SELECT/FROM/WHERE/JOIN using recursive descent parsing. You will add three new parsing functions that extend the grammar. The planner converts the parsed AST into a logical plan tree. You will add two new logical plan nodes: `LogicalAggregate` and `LogicalSort`.

**Query processing pipeline:**
```
SQL string → Lexer → Tokens → Parser → AST → Planner → Logical Plan
```

After this project, the system can parse and plan queries like:
```sql
SELECT department, COUNT(*), AVG(salary)
FROM employees
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY AVG(salary) DESC
```

tasks.title: Parser: GROUP BY
tasks.description: Add parsing for the GROUP BY clause, which appears after WHERE (if present).

functions.name: ParseGroupBy(SelectStatement& stmt)
functions.description:
If the next token is `KW_GROUP`, consume it, expect `KW_BY`, then parse a comma-separated list of column expressions. Add each to the statement via `stmt.AddGroupByExpr()`.

**Grammar:**
```
GROUP BY expr (, expr)*
```

If the next token is not `KW_GROUP`, return without doing anything (GROUP BY is optional).
hints: After consuming GROUP, expect BY with `Expect(TokenType::KW_BY)`.
Parse each expression with `ParsePrimary()` (reuses existing expression parser).

tasks.title: Parser: ORDER BY
tasks.description: Add parsing for the ORDER BY clause, which appears after GROUP BY (or WHERE if no GROUP BY).

functions.name: ParseOrderBy(SelectStatement& stmt)
functions.description:
If the next token is `KW_ORDER`, consume it, expect `KW_BY`, then parse a comma-separated list of sort keys. Each sort key is an expression optionally followed by ASC or DESC (default: ASC). Wrap each in an `OrderByItem` and add to the statement.

**Grammar:**
```
ORDER BY expr [ASC|DESC] (, expr [ASC|DESC])*
```
hints: After parsing the expression, check for KW_ASC or KW_DESC.
Use `stmt.AddOrderByItem(std::move(item))` to add each sort key.

tasks.title: Parser: Aggregate Expressions
tasks.description: Add parsing for aggregate function calls in the SELECT list.

functions.name: ParseAggregateExpr(AggFunc func) → unique_ptr<AggregateExpr>
functions.description:
Parse an aggregate function call. The function keyword (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX) has already been consumed by `ParsePrimary()` and the `AggFunc` type is passed as a parameter. Expect `LPAREN`, parse the argument (or `*` for COUNT), expect `RPAREN`.

**Grammar:**
```
COUNT '(' '*' ')'
COUNT '(' expr ')'
SUM '(' expr ')'
AVG '(' expr ')'
MIN '(' expr ')'
MAX '(' expr ')'
```

tasks.title: Planner: Logical Plan Nodes
tasks.description: Extend the planner to create `LogicalAggregate` and `LogicalSort` nodes when the parsed statement contains GROUP BY/ORDER BY.

functions.name: PlanAggregate(const SelectStatement& stmt, unique_ptr<LogicalPlanNode> child) → unique_ptr<LogicalPlanNode>
functions.description:
If the statement has GROUP BY or contains aggregate functions in the SELECT list, create a `LogicalAggregate` node wrapping the child. Clone the group-by expressions and collect aggregate expressions from the select list.

If there is no aggregation, return the child unchanged.
hints: Use `dynamic_cast<const AggregateExpr*>` to identify aggregate expressions.

functions.name: PlanSort(const SelectStatement& stmt, unique_ptr<LogicalPlanNode> child) → unique_ptr<LogicalPlanNode>
functions.description:
If the statement has ORDER BY, create a `LogicalSort` node wrapping the child. Clone each sort key expression and collect the ascending/descending flags.

If there is no ORDER BY, return the child unchanged.

breakdown.covers: GROUP BY + ORDER BY in same query

testing.note: This project does not depend on Project #1-#3 (no disk I/O). It uses the parser and planner directly.
testing.platforms: macOS or Linux, on either Intel or ARM. On Windows, build inside WSL: a native Windows toolchain is refused, because the reference libraries these downloads carry are built for macOS and Linux only.

hints: Read the existing `ParseSelect()` to understand the parsing flow — your functions are called at the end of it.
Study the `ParseJoinClause()` method as a template for how to add new grammar rules.
GROUP BY and ORDER BY are independent — implement and test them separately.
The aggregate parsing is triggered from `ParsePrimary()` when it detects a keyword like COUNT/SUM. Your `ParseAggregateExpr` receives the function type as a parameter.
For the planner, look at how the existing code creates `LogicalFilter` — your `LogicalAggregate` and `LogicalSort` follow the same wrap-the-child pattern.
The plan tree order is: Scan → Filter → Join → **Aggregate** → **Sort** → Project.

submission.where: Upload the archive to PLMS (https://plms.postech.ac.kr) under Project #4 before the deadline. Submissions sent by email, or left anywhere else, are not collected.
submission.note: Keep the original directory layout inside the archive (src/…), so the files drop straight back into the project tree. Submit only the files you edited: no build/ directory, no compiled objects, no reference libraries.

report.description: What each function you write has to solve, and what the code handed to you for this project does — the parts you read but did not write. The earlier projects are out of scope: they arrive as a compiled library.
The algorithm you chose for each function, and why that one.
Which part of the design is which part of your code, by file and line.
The argument that your code is right.

blocks.text: **For each module below, write one expression that is always true of it** — true before any of its functions is called, and true again every time one of them returns. It may go false in the middle of a function; that is what makes it worth writing down.
The expression is symbols, not words:
If something is hard to put in symbols, define it as a variable in words, then use the variable in the expression:

code: P = the spaces with a car in them
F = the spaces that are empty
for i in 0 .. total_spaces-1:  i in P or i in F

blocks.text: A module holds several such expressions true at once. Pick one and get it right; you do not have to find them all.
**For each function you wrote, show your expression is still true when it returns.** A line or two each, grouped by module.
If a function cannot affect the expression, say so in one line. If it could, say which step keeps it true.
